newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA GO TOP AS BAKERO LEADS ROMP OVER VALLADOLID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA GO TOP AS BAKERO LEADS ROMP OVER VALLADOLID.

text.p: Veteran midfielder Jose Maria Bakero said goodbye to Barcelona fans with a goal as Bobby Robson's side romped their way back to the top of the Spanish first division with a 6-1 win over Valladolid on Monday.
The result leaves Barcelona with 31 points from 13 games, two ahead of Real Madrid.
Barcelona went ahead after 11 minutes when a free-kick from Romanian international Gheorghe Popescu was deflected to give goalkeeper Cesar Sanchez no chance.
Twenty minutes later Ronaldo celebrated his return to league action after a two-week absence by bursting through the defence and side-stepping Sanchez to make it 2-0.
It was the Brazilian's 13th goal in only 11 appearances in the Spanish first division.

Bobby Robson's side went further ahead shortly afterwards when the ball bounced nicely for Luis Enrique Martinez after a one-two with Popescu, and the former Real Madrid man slid the ball home past two defenders.
In the second half Bakero delighted the numerous Barcelona fans carrying banners thanking him for his time at the club by scoring the fourth from a cross by Luis Figo.
The former Spanish international, who was substituted amidst emotional scenes, travels to Mexico on Wednesday to join Veracruz.

Just two minutes after Bakero's farewell Valladolid struck back through Alen Peternac, and Victor Cantatore's side saw a ray of hope immediately afterwards when Barcelona were reduced to ten men as Laurent Blanc received his second yellow card.

But Barcelona refused to rest on their laurels, and Figo headed home the fifth in the 76th minute. In a final ten minutes of end-to-end action substitute Roger Garcia found space down the left and made it six.
